question: Does greater support clipped off the canvas satisfy a necessary condition for the observed Y9 versus X9 training-benefit difference?
scope: Exploratory explanation of already-observed readout results, not independent confirmation, a stereo-geometry claim or new augmentation principle.
preprocess: uint8 gray -> PIL RGB -> bilinear224; matches original input pretransform; no model or labels used for proxy
translation_law: plus and minus equalweight; identity would multiply all losses by2/3 and changes no axis comparison
reference_gray: median of four224-image12x12corner patches; proxy reference, not true background
metrics: fraction of proxy clipped (zero if proxy empty, separately flagged)
clipped continuous squared contrast/whole continuous squared contrast
clipping_convention: X+ loses rightmost9;X- leftmost9;Y+ bottom9;Y- top9; signedlosses averaged
aggregation: within physical object, all36 views then both cameras equally;15 objects are units; report each camera too; no sampling CI or significance claims
necessary_condition: A simple more-content-clipped explanation predicts Y lost support > X consistently. If Y is not larger over the prechosen threshold bank and continuous contrast, do not retain that gross proxy-amount explanation. Small semantic-important pixels, proxy error and CNN boundary/aliasing effects remain unidentified.
display_sample: one preselected source object/category, smallest row among its frozen source grid; both cameras, raw input only
